correctness.rationale: For common \(k,N\), Shannon ranking is the reverse ordering of \(Q=\prod_i n_i^{n_i}\), and order-\(\infty\) Hill diversity is the reverse ordering of \(\max_i n_i\). After subtracting the baseline one individual per species, profiles are partitions of \(r=N-k\); once \(k\ge r\), padding by ones proves stabilization. Exact enumeration gives the stated \(r=4\) weak boundary and \(r=6\) strict boundary with the complete first layer.

value.rationale: Shannon and reciprocal Berger–Parker are canonical order-\(1\) and order-\(\infty\) Hill diversities, respectively, and differ maximally in how much of the abundance distribution they use. By fixing richness and expressing census size as baseline plus excess, the theorem isolates the smallest amount of compositional heterogeneity needed for a genuine cross-order ranking reversal and classifies every minimal mechanism.
